source_construct: L711: tag["name"][1:].lower() for a TaggedOutboxObject's tag
target_translation: strings.ToLower(name[1:]) is the slice, with pyLower in place of strings.ToLower (see below). The name can hold any Unicode word characters (\w), but the slice only drops its first character, which is always the ASCII "#", so a byte index of 1 equals a character index of 1. Only Hashtag tags reach this line; their name is "#" + the match of _HASHTAG_REGEX, already lowercased. Note for the implementer: Python's str.lower differs from strings.ToLower for U+0130 ("İ" becomes "i" + U+0307) and for final sigma; the markdownify row of the exact_output batch covers it.

source_construct: L75: v[1 : len(v) - 1] strips the quotes of a Signature parameter value
target_translation: Byte slicing is exact here, but it needs a guard: if len(v) >= 2 { out[k] = v[1:len(v)-1] } else { out[k] = "" }. Python gives "" for v of length 0 or 1 (keyId= or keyId=x), where Go's v[1:len(v)-1] panics. Bytes are right because Starlette decodes header values as latin-1, one character per byte, and net/http keeps the raw bytes: dropping the first and last byte in Go drops the first and last character in Python. The value is remote input, not checked for quotes.
